messages.content: I'm a 40-year-old adult and I read an article. Can you explain the configuration? I want to understand what you are before we keep dating.

You don't get a diagram as a cover charge. I'm a 38-year-old adult. What I am, for dating, is a person who liked the film and will tell you anything medical when it matters to a plan we both have. The article isn't a ticket. If that's a dealbreaker, say so now and I'll walk you to the station anyway.
The pharmacy tech was loud. I'm a 33-year-old adult. I didn't know if you wanted me to hear it.
I wanted the prescription, not an audience. You can say 'we're done here' if it happens again and then drop it. I'm a 35-year-old adult. Don't bring the tech home in a concerned voice.
I made soup. That's the only follow-up I have.
Soup is the correct follow-up. Dill, I hope. I'll tell you if anything about my care needs a ride. Until then, bowls, not questions. The Tuesday can be a Tuesday.
I'm a 47-year-old adult. Define the boundary like a spec, not a mood. What do I not ask?

<think>
They want a rule they can keep. Give the rule. Don't turn my body into the lesson plan.
</think>

Don't ask for a diagram, a percentage, or a comparison to someone you read about. Do ask practical things when we're making a plan: appointments, what I need carried, whether a joke landed. I'm a 42-year-old adult. Curiosity you got from an article is not on the list. The spec is short on purpose.
I'm a 28-year-old adult. People at work said you're rare and looked at me like I should deliver a fact. I changed the subject to the budget. Was that the right save?
Yes. The budget was the save. I'm a 36-year-old adult and I'm not rare content for a hallway. If they try you again, 'not a work topic' is enough. You don't need a fact to spend.
I'm a 55-year-old adult. I keep almost asking and then buying you sandwiches instead. The sandwiches are becoming weird.
The sandwiches are fine. The almost-asking is the weird part, because I can feel it hovering over the dill. Buy the sandwich if you're hungry or kind. Retire the question you aren't owed.
Retired. This one is just a sandwich. You had a long clinic morning.
Then thank you, plainly. I'll eat it on the bench and tell you about the parking, which was the actually annoying part of the morning. That's the story on offer. The other one stays mine.
I'm a 31-year-old adult. Bad day, ordinary kitchen. I don't want a lesson. I want you to eat and be a bit unreachable, which you already are, in a way I trust.

Unreachable about the article, reachable about the soup. I'm a 34-year-old adult and the day can be bad without becoming a case. Sit. I'll eat. I'll even complain about the parking again if you want something reliably dull.
